events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The booking is an immediate RydeX order and the cancellation record shows the rider cancelled 3 min 1 s (181 s) after acceptance at 09:00:10, with $6.61 on record as the cancellation fee [F3][F6]. NS-0 routes a rider-cancelled immediate booking to NS-4, and NS-4 charges $6.61 only where cancellation comes after the 3-minute grace period; 181 s exceeds 180 s, so the fee is due [F3][NS-0][NS-4].

The driver did press "I'm Here" (F5), which the rider side says pulls the fee into NS-1 [F5][NS-1]. But NS-1 and NS-2 are conditioned on the driver cancelling while alleging a rider no-show: NS-0 branches to NS-1/NS-2 only when cancelled_by = driver, and here cancelled_by = rider [F3][NS-0]. A driver's "I'm Here" tap by itself does not convert the rider's own late cancellation into a no-show case, so NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) never become requirements and NS-2's full refund is not triggered [F3][NS-1][NS-2]. The rider advocate's own rebuttal to D1 concedes the timing test under NS-4 is met [F3][NS-4].

The rider's complaint that she was "two minutes away" and then "held up upstairs" is narrative only; F8 records no in-app chat at all, and no message with a timestamp exists [F8]. That narrative fails as a defence: NS-4 gives no free-cancellation right merely because the rider was slow to reach the pick-up, and NS-7's discretion route is a recommendation, not a ground to defeat a fee that is validly charged [F8][NS-4][NS-7].

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice" is contradicted by the system records: first entry within 200 m of the pick-up at 09:02:40, closest approach 39 m at 09:03:00, and cancellation 31 s after recorded arrival [F9][F1][F2][F4]. System records override statements, so the driver's wait claim fails [F9][NS-1]. That issue does not change the outcome, because the fee stands on the rider's own late cancellation under NS-4, not on any verified wait [F3][F6][NS-4].

Amount: no sum is refunded. The only figure in a fare fact is $6.61, the fee validly charged after the 3-minute grace period, so no refund arithmetic applies and the amount is null [F3][F6][NS-4].

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: This is an immediate (RydeX) booking cancelled by the rider 3 min 1 s after matching, i.e. beyond the 3-minute grace window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee falls to be tested under NS-4 and, the driver having asserted a rider no-show, under NS-1.

The driver's no-show claim fails NS-1(iii): the platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40 and the trip was cancelled at 09:03:11, only 31 s later, and GPS shows just 30 s cumulative time within 200 m of the pickup before cancellation — far short of the required continuous 3 min 1 s / > 180 s.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 and remained within 200 m for only 11 s afterwards, so the continuous-wait requirement of NS-1(iii) is not met even measured from the tap (which was itself 39 m from the pickup point, within the 200 m arrival radius).

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice" (F9) is contradicted by the system records and is not corroborated by any in-app chat, since the chat record contains no messages at all; system records prevail over the statement.
Because at least one of the NS-1 conditions (i)(ii)(iii) fails, the whole cancellation fee must be refunded to the rider, i.e. $6.61 as recorded in the fare facts.

No safety escalation is warranted: the only statements on record are the driver's factual no-show claim and no message, statement or complaint contains any threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation.
The $6.61 refund is not barred by the 30-day dispute window, the rider having filed this dispute in the ordinary course for this trip, and it should be issued as a Ryde voucher.

weaknesses: The rider admits she was "held up upstairs" and cancelled rather than boarding, and her own message that she was "two minutes away" is not in the record (F8 shows no chat messages), so the driver can argue the cancellation was the rider's own doing; NS-1/NS-2 nevertheless govern because the fee requires the specific verified-wait conditions, which fail on F2/F4/F5.

The rider cancelled 3 min 1 s after matching (F3), one second past the NS-4 free window, so the driver will argue the fee is simply due as a late rider cancellation; our answer is that the driver pressed "I'm Here" and alleged a no-show, which pulls the fee into the stricter NS-1 test that the timeline (F4, F5) and GPS (F2) records break.

The driver's own history is clean (F14: rating 4.9, 0 disputes), which may lend weight to his 6-minute claim (F9) against the GPS timeline; we rely on NS-1's requirement that the system records control.

claims.assertion: The rider herself cancelled the booking (cancelled by rider at 09:03:11, i.e. 3 min 1 s after acceptance at 09:00:10), so this is a rider-cancellation case: the $6.61 on record is payable only if the grace period under NS-4 has expired, which it has by one second (>3:00).

The rider's own message concedes she caused the failure — she told the driver she was two minutes away, got held up upstairs and then cancelled — so the trip failed because the rider did not come to the pick-up point, not because the driver failed to arrive; the driver was on scene from early on.

The driver did in fact reach the pick-up point: platform records arrival at 09:02:40 and his closest approach was 39 m at 09:03:00, and he was within 200 m of the pick-up from 09:02:40 until the rider cancelled at 09:03:11 — so the rider's cancellation was not excused by any driver-side failure to show up (NS-8's late-ETA waiver does not exist in Ryde policy).

No condition of NS-2 is triggered: the free-waiting / grace mechanic the rider effectively invokes only removes the fee where the driver never arrived or cancelled himself, and here the rider was the cancelling party within the paid window, so the $6.61 stands and the correct outcome is no_action.

The driver's account has 1600 days of history, a 4.9 rating and 700 trips in 90 days with zero disputes and zero upheld complaints, while the rider has 3 disputes in 90 days; there is no basis for any account flag against the driver under RD-6 or NS-2, and no safety issue requiring escalation under SAFE-1/SAFE-2.

weaknesses: The driver's post-trip statement (F9) claims he "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice", but the system records contradict it: he first came within 200 m of the pick-up at 09:02:40 (F2) and his closest approach was 39 m at 09:03:00 (F1), so the wait at the pick-up was only about 31 seconds (F2, F4). The rider's side will use F8/F9 to argue the driver's account is unreliable.

The gap between the $6.61 threshold and the cancellation is only one second: accepted 09:00:10, cancelled 09:03:11 = 3 min 1 s (F3). The rider will argue the fee is a technicality and press NS-7's 30-day waiver / discretion route for a voucher.
No in-app chat exists (F8) and the driver's version appears only in his after-the-fact statement (F9), which under the rules is a claim, not evidence that beats the GPS/timeline records (F1, F2, F4).

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 and stayed within 200 m for only 11 s after the tap (F5), so this record cannot be used to support the $5.00 waiting fee under NS-6, nor any 'waited more than 3 minutes' assertion; the case must stand on the rider-cancellation branch NS-4, not NS-1.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: the fee's timing test under NS-4 is met by one second (accepted 09:00:10, cancelled 09:03:11, F3). But that branch is displaced here because the driver pressed "I'm Here" (F5) and asserted a rider no-show, which routes the fee through NS-0 to NS-1, whose conditions are not satisfied (see D3/D4).

The rider's supposed message is not in the record — F8 states there are no in-app messages at all — so the only thing before the judge is the complaint narrative; and in any event NS-1 does not ask why the rider did not board, it asks whether the driver verified arrival and waited continuously past the threshold, which the system records show he did not (F2, F4, F5).

Arrival alone is not enough: NS-1 requires the driver to press "I'm Here" and then wait continuously at the pick-up point beyond the threshold, and the records show he was within 200 m for only 30 s cumulatively before cancellation (F2) and stayed in range only 11 s after his 09:03:00 tap (F5), with cancellation 31 s after the recorded arrival (F4) — so the wait condition fails regardless of NS-8.

NS-2 is squarely triggered: where any of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is not met the $6.61 is refunded in full, and (iii) fails on F2/F4/F5; the driver's own admission that the wait at the stand was only about 31 s confirms the same fact pattern he cannot escape.

We seek no account flag and no safety escalation, so this point is uncontested; the driver's clean profile (F14) is irrelevant to whether NS-1's wait conditions were met, and the rider's own dispute history (F13) is not a basis for deciding this case.

Accepted: the booking is an immediate RydeX order cancelled by the rider 3 min 1 s after acceptance, so NS-4 (not NS-1) is the operative test — the free window is 3 minutes and the rider cancelled one second past it, making the $6.61 due.

Void as framed: NS-1 only governs where the driver cancels alleging a rider no-show, but the cancellation record shows cancelled_by = rider (F3), so NS-1(iii) never becomes a requirement and cannot defeat the fee; the rider's own cancellation is tested under NS-4 alone.

This cuts against the rider, not the driver: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pick-up point, i.e. inside the arrival radius (F5, F1), so the rider cancelled 11 s after the driver confirmed presence at the pick-up while she was still upstairs — the delay was hers, not the driver's.

Conceded in part: the driver's "6 minutes / called twice" statement (F9) is not corroborated and is outweighed by the GPS and timeline records (F1, F2, F4); the driver's case does not rely on it, because the fee stands on the rider's own late cancellation (F3) under NS-4.

Contested: NS-2's refund follows only when the driver cancels alleging a no-show, which the record does not show — cancelled_by = rider at 3 min 1 s (F3), past the 3-minute window, so the $6.61 is properly charged and no_action is the correct outcome.

Agreed, no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation applies; the record contains no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, and the driver's account history (4.4 years, 4.9 rating, 700 trips, 0 disputes) gives no ground for any flag, so both sides should accept a clean, non-escalated ruling.

The 30-day window is not in issue, but the manifest inequity is one second: the rider cancelled at 09:03:11, 3 min 1 s after acceptance (F3), and the policy gives no discretion to waive a fee where the rider's own late cancellation caused the failed trip while the driver was waiting at the pick-up (F1, F5).
